Winter

The air in the Grand Culinary Arena was thick with the scent of vanilla and anxiety. It was the final round of the National Baking Championship, and Kevin, a contestant whose confidence far exceeded his culinary intuition, stood before his masterpiece: The Velvet Cloud Cake.

Kevin reached for the sugar bowl. His hand, trembling from the pressure of the live broadcast, bypassed the white granules and clamped down on the coarse, crystalline salt. He poured. He mixed. He baked. He smiled.

When the cakes were presented to the judges, the head judge, a stern woman named Madame Gable, took a bite of Kevin’s cake. Her face didn’t just drop; it underwent a geological shift. She chewed. She swallowed. She stared into the middle distance as if trying to remember the concept of joy.

"It is... bold," Madame Gable said, her voice tight. "Very bold."

Kevin, panic rising in his throat like bile, saw the other contestants looking at their own creations with similar dread. One had accidentally used soy sauce instead of chocolate syrup. Another had substituted baking soda for baking powder, creating a cake that tasted like metallic pennies and regret.

"Actually," Kevin blurted out, sweating profusely. "This is a new trend. Savory Desserts. It’s all the rage in Paris. We’re exploring the umami-sweet dichotomy."

The other bakers, sensing a lifeline, nodded vigorously. "Yes!" cried Sarah, holding up her soy-chocolate monstrosity. "It’s avant-garde."

Madame Gable raised an eyebrow. "Avant-garde. I see."

The tasting session that followed was a masterclass in polite horror. Judge #2, a man who loved sugar, took a bite of Kevin’s salt cake. He closed his eyes, not in pleasure, but in a desperate attempt to dissociate from the reality of the sodium bomb in his mouth.

"The texture is... crisp," Judge #2 managed, his voice cracking. "The salinity really cuts through the richness of the... whatever this is."

"It’s a sea-salt caramel profile," Kevin lied, his soul leaving his body.

Judge #3 tasted Sarah’s soy-chocolate cake. He paused for a full ten seconds. The silence was deafening. Finally, he spoke. "It has a distinct... oceanic finish. Very briny. I can taste the fish."
